candidates.title: File:Clay Pot from Liloan 1.jpg
candidates.author: Bim24
candidates.description: The clay pot from Liloan, Cebu is a traditional pottery piece that is part of Cebu's rich cultural heritage. Clay pottery in Cebu, particularly from towns like Liloan, is known for its craftsmanship and long-standing tradition passed down through generations. In Liloan, clay pots are used for a variety of purposes, including cooking, storage, and even for ceremonial or decorative purposes. These pots are handmade, with local artisans using traditional techniques that have been refined over many years. The clay is carefully shaped, often using a spinning wheel, and then fired in a kiln to harden it. The finished product is sometimes decorated with simple but beautiful designs. At The Kabilin Center, these clay pots are showcased in exhibits to highlight their cultural significance, demonstrating the artistry and craftsmanship of Cebuano potters. These pots also represent the connection between local communities and their traditional practices, as they have been a part of daily life for centuries.

candidates.title: File:The built in flash of a SLR camera, Pentax MZ-30, firing 1.jpg
candidates.author: W.carter
candidates.description: The built in flash of a SLR camera, Pentax MZ-30, firing. A reflector was set up in front of the Pentax camera in a dark room. The camera taking the photo was set up much the same way you do when photographing lightning at night: on a tripod, manual focus and long shutter time. The Pentax was activated using its timer function, and the camera making the photo was triggered just before the flash would fire from the Pentax. This way, the flash bounced off the reflector and illuminated the camera enough to be exposed by its own flash, and the other camera was able to register both the flash firing and the Pentax in one long-exposure photo. Studio photography in Tuntorp, Brastad, Lysekil Municipality, Sweden.
